newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slightly down in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares slightly down in early bourse trade.

text.p: German shares were slightly down in early bourse trade on Wednesday, hurt a bit by overnight weakness on Wall Street but still resilient after the recent run-up to record levels.
The 30-share DAX index was down 0.81 points at 2,627.27 and confined to a relatively narrow trading range as the market struggled to find direction after the hectic start to the week.
"It seems nobody is in a mood to commit to anything today. I think this market's going sideways," said a Munich dealer.
"People are drawing some breath after Monday," said a Frankfurt dealer, referring to the market's record heights reached earlier this week.
Dealers noted that the German market seemed relatively stable at the current very high levels and said a further upward push could not be ruled out be the end of the week.
Prices might also be influenced by the expiry Friday of futures and options contracts on the DAX index, which can prompt a sharp jump in the cash market, dealers said.
Stock index futures helped lead stocks higher this week as dealers rushed to cover short positions following a general rally on world stock markets.
Among individual stocks, carmaker Volkswagen AG stood out slightly in early trade as it rose 95 pfennigs to 574.75 marks in healthy volumes.
One dealer attributed the rise to news of the company's plan to substitute special certificates for cash payments for overtime.
Sportswear maker Adidas AG was among the top percentage losers, falling five marks to 133.50 on profit-taking after recent run-up to new record high at 140 marks.
